payload.name: Preserve-specific-facts-when-enriching-event-memories
payload.description: When updating an existing event memory with new context, preserve previously stored specific facts (exact type, date, or status) unless the new message explicitly contradicts them; merge new details instead of replacing the original ones.
content: Before updating an existing event memory, compare its stored facts with the new message. Keep any stored fact that is more specific or has a clear timestamp unless the new message explicitly contradicts it.
When new information adds context to an earlier event (e.g., cause, activity, or treatment), merge that context without overwriting the original event type or onset date.
Set world_start to the original event date unless the new evidence clearly establishes a different event or a revised date.

solves: An enrichment UPDATE can overwrite a correctly stored specific event fact (type and date) with a broader later description, losing details needed for future questions. The failure mechanism is replacing precise prior facts during non-contradictory context addition. This skill applies to any UPDATE of an existing event memory where new information adds cause, activity, or treatment but does not explicitly contradict the original fact; it instructs merging so original specifics and timestamp survive.
